Study_Title: Banking Fraud Intention and Behavior Study - Section A: Demographics and Control Variables (T1)

Variables.Notes: Auto-generated, unique for each participant

Variables.Description: Date and time of data collection
Variables.Notes: Timestamp for each survey response
Core variable for comparative analysis. Balanced sample (n=500 each)
Text label for Country variable
Distribution skewed towards younger adults (gamma distribution). Controls for developmental and generational differences.

Variables.Distribution: ~52% Male, ~46% Female, ~2% Other/Prefer not to say
Variables.Notes: Inclusive coding following best practices. Controls for gender differences in technology adoption and risk perception.
Text label for Gender variable
Correlated with age and income. Controls for digital literacy and comprehension of financial information.
Text label for Education variable
Correlated with education and age. Country-specific currency bands provided separately. Controls for financial resources and access to banking services.
Text label for Income_Level variable
Currency-specific income bands for Nigeria. Based on 2025 economic data.
Currency-specific income bands for Ghana. Based on 2025 economic data.
Digital bank users may face different security controls and fraud exposure patterns. Correlated with age, education, and income. Digital banking more prevalent in Nigeria.
Text label for Bank_Type variable

Variables.Description: Years of having a bank account
Variables.Notes: Correlated with age and bank type. Digital bank accounts are newer (max ~8 years). Longer tenure increases exposure to fraud attempts.
Correlated with bank type (digital users more frequent), income, and age. Higher frequency increases exposure to fraud risks.
Text label for Frequency_of_Use variable

Variables.Description: Previous experience as a victim of bank fraud
Variables.Question: Have you ever been a victim of bank fraud?
Variables.Notes: Powerful predictor of both intention and behavior. Correlated with frequency of use, years with account, and bank type. Overall rate ~20-30% (realistic for West African markets).
Text label for Past_Victim variable

Data_Quality_Notes: All correlations are realistic and theoretically justified
Outliers: Age and Years_with_Account are constrained to realistic ranges
Distribution checks: All variables follow expected patterns for West African banking populations
Sampling_Strategy: Balanced sampling across countries (n=500 each). Realistic distributions based on demographic profiles of banking populations in Nigeria and Ghana.
Ethical_Considerations: Inclusive gender coding, culturally appropriate income bands, consent assumed for fabricated data.
Recommended_Analyses: Independent t-tests for continuous variables (Nigeria vs Ghana)
Logistic regression with Past_Victim as outcome
